# Moodle CLI 0.10.0

This release adds `moodle sync`, which keeps a local folder per unit up to date, and `moodle coverage`, which checks every command against your own Moodle site. You can now set up the remote MCP server entirely from a cloud session. `grades` returns compact, paged output, and page readers handle more sites: other languages, Classic, Moodle 4.4+, and restricted activities.

## Highlights

- **Introducing `moodle sync`.** One folder per unit stays in step with Moodle, and a file you edited is never overwritten.
- **Introducing `moodle coverage`.** It runs each read-only command once against your units and checks every answer against a second source on the site.
- **Set up the remote MCP server from a cloud session.** No local terminal, no desktop browser and no hand-made Cloudflare token.
- **`grades` is compact by default.** It returns marked items without feedback, at most 20 rows per call. On a real five-unit gradebook the default response is a third of its old size.
- **Readers follow the site's language.** They use the site's own wording for the labels they look for, so non-English sites and customised strings read correctly.
- **A restricted activity is reported as restricted.** It is no longer read as the course page.

## `moodle sync`

`moodle sync` mirrors each unit's resources, folder contents and assignment attachments into one folder per unit, laid out by section. Pages and books are saved as single HTML files with their images embedded, so they read the same offline.

```bash
moodle sync --to ~/Units              # every unit, one subfolder each
moodle sync UNIT --to ~/Units         # just one
moodle sync --dry-run                 # what would change, nothing written
```

Each unit folder holds a `.moodle-sync.json` manifest. A rerun asks Moodle only whether each file changed, so it usually downloads nothing. The rules for your files:
- A changed file replaces your copy only if you have not edited it.
- An edited copy stays put, and the new version lands beside it as `name (updated YYYY-MM-DD).ext`.
- Files removed from Moodle are reported and kept.
- A file you delete stays deleted until Moodle changes it.
- You can rename or move a unit folder freely: the manifest, not the folder name, says which unit it holds.

The rules also hold when a run is interrupted:
- Ctrl+C or a fatal error still saves the manifest, so the next run doesn't mistake an untouched file for an edit.
- A unit that fails to load is reported, and the other units carry on.
- On drives without hard links, such as exFAT or FAT USB sticks and some network shares, files are copied instead, and an existing file is still never replaced.
- Names that Windows reserves (`CON`, `NUL`, `COM1` and the rest) get a `_` suffix.
- Names such as `../` never leave the unit folder.

## `moodle coverage`

Moodle sites differ: some disable web services, and themes, languages and course formats change the pages the CLI reads. `moodle coverage` uses your signed-in session to run each read-only command once against your own units. It prints one line per command as it finishes.

A command passes only if its answer agrees with an independent source on the site:
- The unit's contents check names, units and files.
- The calendar checks due dates.
- The quiz page, its review page and the gradebook check grades against each other.
- The forum listing checks subjects and search.

A contradiction shows as `≠`. Content that was fetched but not understood shows as `?`. Either one, or an outright failure, exits with code 3.

The first line names the CLI version, whether it is the latest, and the runtime; a failure on an old release may already be fixed, so run `moodle update` before reporting one. `moodle coverage --json` adds the Moodle release, theme, and the services the site disables. It holds counts, ids and error messages, not your name or your unit titles, so you can attach it to an issue.

Coverage creates nothing and never submits. Moodle logs the pages it opens as views, just as it does when you browse them, and it can mark forum posts read.

## Set up the remote MCP server from a cloud session

An agent in a sandbox can now run `moodle mcp deploy --remote-login --yes --json` with no Moodle session on the machine.
- Cloudflare sign-in uses Wrangler's device flow. The CLI prints the `dash.cloudflare.com` link, and you approve it in your own browser.
- The deploy returns the `endpoint` and a one-time `setupUrl`, valid for 10 minutes. Open it yourself and sign in to Moodle inside Cloudflare Browser Run; the Worker validates that session and pins your Moodle account as its owner. The agent should hand the link over unchanged and never open it.
- Add the `endpoint` as a custom connector. The approval page recognises you as the owner, or offers **Sign in with Moodle** again.

Several things changed alongside this:
- **A Worker without a Moodle session still answers MCP.** `initialize` and `tools/list` work, so hosted clients no longer show a broken connector. Tool calls return `MOODLE_AUTH_REQUIRED` with a link to sign in.
- **Owner sign-in is guarded.** One attempt runs at a time. A Worker nobody has claimed accepts a sign-in only with a pairing code, and a different Moodle account is always refused. A daily launch budget stops strangers from using up the free plan's browser minutes.
- **`moodle mcp pair` also prints the setup link.**
- **The first deploy on a fresh machine works.** Wrangler reports a signed-out machine in a way the CLI did not recognise, so every first deploy failed with "Wrangler command failed".

## Session renewal

- **One probe now tells every part of the CLI how a session renews.** The mobile-app token is the only renewal that needs nobody, so it wins wherever the site offers it. Otherwise renewal falls back to signing in. `moodle auth status` shows both `mobile_service` and `renewal`.
- **A working mobile token is no longer dropped by a network blip.** Previously, an unreachable Moodle, a proxy or maintenance page answering in its place, or Moodle's per-user rate limit all looked like a revoked token. Now only Moodle's own refusal counts as revoked; anything else keeps the token for the next try.
- **Renewal can't stall tool calls.** Minting a session and capturing a token each have a 30-second deadline, so a Moodle that stops answering no longer holds every waiting tool call.

## `grades` is compact by default

A gradebook can hold dozens of ungraded interactive items and long marker feedback, and `grades` used to copy all of it into every answer. In both the CLI and MCP, it now returns marked items without feedback by default:

- `mode: "summary"` (`--mode summary`) gives per-unit counts and Moodle's course totals.
- `mode: "all"` (`--mode all`), or `include_ungraded`, adds ungraded items.
- `include_feedback` (`--include-feedback`) adds marker feedback. `item` still gives one task's feedback with its rubric.
- `types` (`--types assign,quiz`) filters by Moodle module, read from the activity link, so translated labels don't matter. `assignment` is accepted as `assign`.
- Detail responses return at most 20 rows across units. Use `limit` and `offset` to page through them; `matched`, `returned` and `has_more` show where you are.

On a real five-unit gradebook the default response went from 6,491 to 2,170 characters, still in a single call.

**This changes the default response.** An MCP client that relied on getting every row with feedback should pass `mode: "all", include_feedback: true` and page through the results. `graded_only` and `--graded-only` still work.

## Page readers

- **Site language.** One `core_get_strings` call per session fetches the site's own wording for the labels the assignment, quiz and review readers look for. German sites, and sites that renamed labels such as "Submission status", now read correctly.
- **Restricted and hidden activities.** Moodle answers an activity you can see but not open by redirecting to the course page. `item` and `activities show` used to read that page as the activity, with the course's name and another assignment's due date. All six readers now say `Activity N is not available to you`, followed by Moodle's reason.
- **Moodle 4.4+.** A section link in the breadcrumb no longer overwrites the course id.
- **Classic theme.** Activities are no longer named after their course, including when the course's full name matches its short name.
- **Graders without a picture.** Their initials are no longer glued onto their name.
- **Young sites.** Section 1 is no longer dropped when section 0's id is 1.
- **Links.** Links are read with `forceview=1`, so a link set to open directly is no longer parsed as its target page.

## Units, due dates and tables

- **`moodle 101` opens activity 101.** It used to open the unit coded LAB101. A bare number names a unit only by its id or its whole code. `16` is unit 16, not a unit coded LAB160. `moodle open 101` had the same bug.
- **Due dates on sites without the timeline.** When a site disables the timeline calendar, `due`, the MCP `due` tool and the dashboard read each unit's calendar instead. If one unit's calendar fails, the whole list fails, so a deadline list never silently leaves out a unit.
- **More screens use tables.** `moodle UNIT`, `due`, `find`, section views and `home` now print tables, with the ID first because it's what the next command takes. Long names are cut to the terminal width.

## Updates and the toolchain

- **`moodle update` installs the exact release it checked**, into the npm prefix that holds the running copy. A lagging npm mirror can no longer install an older build, and an npm from another Node on your PATH can no longer update a different install.
- **A standalone binary is verified before it replaces the old one.** It must run and report the expected version, so a truncated download or a proxy error page can't break a working executable.
- **Wrangler 4.145.0.** It clears the undici advisories that `npm audit` flagged. The Wrangler the CLI downloads for the MCP Worker is pinned to the same version.

## Upgrade

```bash
npm install -g moodle-cli@0.10.0
```

Or:

```bash
moodle update
```

`moodle update` also redeploys a managed MCP Worker. The Worker needs the redeploy to get the new `grades` contract, renewal handling and owner sign-in. No configuration or cache format changes; sync manifests are new and live in your unit folders.
